contributions.headingText: Well-differentiated papillary mesothelial tumour (WDPMT) of the pleura is a neoplasm of mesothelial origin composed of papillary stromal formations covered by bland mesothelial cells lacking invasion.
2C26.0 & XH85T6 Mesothelioma of pleura & Well-differentiated papillary mesothelioma of the pleura
Not recommended: well-differentiated papillary mesothelioma; benign papillary mesothelioma.
WDPMT arises from the visceral and/or parietal pleura.
Patients with WDPMT commonly present with dyspnoea. Unilateral pleural effusion is frequent and often recurrent. Some tumours are discovered incidentally.

With fewer than 50 cases reported, pleural WDPMT is less common than its counterpart in the peritoneum and far rarer than pleural diffuse mesothelioma. Pleural WDPMT shows no apparent sex predilection and occurs over a wide age range (median age: ~62 years) {11688466; 15087673; 23530588; 30419426}.
The etiology remains uncertain. Although asbestos exposure has been documented in some patients, the rarity of WDPMT poses challenges to conducting epidemiological studies {11688466; 15087673}.

Pathogenic mechanisms of WDPMT have not been established. A BAP1 germline mutation has rarely been detected {23585512}. CDKN2A homozygous deletion has not been observed in pleural WDPMT {29763720; 24618613}.
Tumours protrude from the pleura as single arborescent masses as large as 50 mm or as multifocal nodules < 10 mm that stud the pleura and impart a granular to velvety appearance {11688466; 15087673}.

The tumour arises from the pleural surface as distinct thin to broad papillary formations covered by a single layer of flattened to cuboidal bland mesothelial cells with inconspicuous nucleoli, rare to absent mitoses, and no stromal invasion. The papillae consist of paucicellular myxoid or fibrovascular cores devoid of inflammation that infrequently show hyalinization and occasionally contain foamy macrophages. Psammomatous calcifications are rare. Papillae infrequently exhibit compressive crowding, in which back-to-back arrangements simulate invasion, but keratin staining demonstrates maintained papillary architecture {24618613}.

Immunohistochemistry

WDPMT stains with mesothelial markers {29763720} (see section Diffuse pleural mesothelioma).

Differential diagnosis

The diagnosis of WDPMT requires histological examination of the entire tumour to exclude invasion. Principal differential considerations include mesothelial proliferations with the histological appearance of WDPMT that show focal invasion, reactive mesothelial hyperplasia, and diffuse mesothelioma (see #14051Table 2.01). Rarely, mesothelial proliferations with the architecture of WDPMT invade the papillary cores and/or focally invade the submesothelial connective tissue as bland tubules or solid foci of epithelioid or spindle cells {24618613}. It has not been established whether such lesions, which have been referred to as well-differentiated papillary mesothelioma with invasive foci, are best considered a subtype of WDPMT, represent early diffuse mesothelioma, or are a distinct entity. Nor have invasive size and depth criteria been defined. The mesothelium in reactive pleuritis occasionally forms papillae, but unlike those of WDPMT, the papillae are stubby and have reactive cytological features and accompanying inflammation. Epithelioid diffuse mesothelioma with papillary growth can bear a striking resemblance to WDPMT, but it is distinguished by invasion into the deep pleural connective tissue or beyond.
Cytological samples are not relevant to the diagnosis of WDPMT, because invasion cannot be excluded.
Molecular data are extremely limited. BAP1 is usually retained {29763720}.

Essential:

  • Papillary stromal formations covered by bland mesothelium
  • No stromal invasion

Desirable:

  • Immunohistochemical staining for mesothelial markers
  • BAP1 positivity retained

Although a minority of cases follow a benign clinical course after complete resection, most WDPMTs are characterized by slow growth of recurrent disease, with extended survival of several years or longer {11688466; 15087673}. For this reason, and to avoid confusion with diffuse mesothelioma, the designation “well-differentiated papillary mesothelial tumour”, rather than the historical term “well-differentiated papillary mesothelioma”, is recommended. Mesothelial proliferations with the appearance of WDPMT that show focal invasion have a propensity for multifocality and recurrence, but they are rarely fatal {24618613}.

Whether pleural WDPMT is a precursor of diffuse mesothelioma is unresolved {24118858}. Exceptional cases of pleural WDPMT with concomitant or subsequent diffuse mesothelioma show BAP1 loss in both neoplasms, raising the possibility of a clonal relationship {29763720}.
